newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks strong in morning on firm U.S. markets.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks strong in morning on firm U.S. markets.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks traded higher on Friday morning, boosted by strong gains in U.S. stocks and remarks by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan.
"It started with the Dow Jones up 83 points and then Greenspan's speech was very positive," said Priscilla Ng, executive director at CEF GC Brokerage Ltd.
The Hang Seng index of blue chip stocks was up 85.48 points at 13,373.88. Turnover was HK$2.25 billion after the first hour of trade.
Overnight the Dow Industrials climbed 83.12 points to 6823.86.
Dealers said comments by Greenspan fuelled a broad-based rally in U.S. stocks, lifting the average up within reach of its all-time closing high of 6,883.90 set on January 21.

Greenspan told the State Finance Committee that the consumer price index is overstated by 0.5 to 1.5 points a year, but the Fed takes that into account in policy debates. He also said policymakers consider exchange rates when deciding monetary policy and noted a stronger dollar keeps import prices lower.
"He basically said there's no inflation worry," Ng said. "I think the overhang of interest rates should be resolved at (next week's Fed policy) meeting. There won't be a rate rise."
Property stocks staged a strong recovery, with the property sub-index rising 151.13 points to 25,319.39.
Cheung Kong Holdings and Great Eagle Holdings led the charge, with Cheung Kong up HK$0.75 at HK$73.25 and Great Eagle HK$0.70 higher at HK$32.10.

Traders said they were watching GZI Transport for further strength following the new listing's closing price on Thursday of HK$4.875 against an issue price of HK$3.23. The stock was trading HK$0.075 weaker at HK$4.80 at mid-morning.
Bank of East Asia was trading down HK$0.30 at HK$35.50 despite expectations of strong earnings on Monday.
Hongkong Telecom was unchanged at HK$13.25 following news that, in partnership with a computer company, it had won one of two national paging licenses in Taiwan.
